record.what_it_does: Lark (Larksuite) is ByteDance's international workplace suite: chat, docs, calendar, email, approvals, and a developer open platform.
record.auth_notes: Apps have an App ID and App Secret. These are exchanged for a tenant_access_token (app identity, scoped by the app's permissions) or an app_access_token (used for marketplace apps). OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow gives a user_access_token (user identity). A multi-user agent toolkit would use OAuth2 user_access_token with a refresh token. The tenant token suits bot actions. The docs call tenant_access_token and user_access_token the two main credentials; app_access_token and the exact OAuth endpoints were not verified on a fetched page.
record.access_notes: Anyone can create a custom app for free, and developers can debug with their own user_access_token without publishing. Custom-app permissions need approval from the tenant admin. To let other tenants install an app, it must be a store app, which needs a Lark open-platform launch review and a tenant install review. I did not find a pricing page, so I can't confirm whether a free Lark tenant is limited.
record.api_breadth_notes: Covers messaging (im), contacts, calendar, docs, drive, base, sheets, approval, mail, VC, HR and more. I estimate well over 500 endpoints; I did not count them. Official SDKs exist for Go, Node, Java and Python.
record.mcp_notes: npm package @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp, from github.com/larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp. It runs over stdio or SSE, is in Beta, and supports --oauth user tokens and the --domain https://open.larksuite.com option. I found no vendor-hosted remote MCP URL.
record.blocker_notes: The API is public and creating a custom app is self-serve. Distributing one OAuth app to many external tenants requires store-app publication, which has a platform review plus a tenant-admin install review. Permission scopes also need admin approval. Lark and Feishu run on separate domains (open.larksuite.com vs open.feishu.cn).
